### Question:
Need to decide between `uv add --dev poetry` and `uv tool install poetry` for a service that ships in a slim Docker image. Show me.

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev poetry

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install poetry
```

`uv add --dev` makes `poetry` part of what `uv sync` reconstructs for every contributor. `uv tool install` installs it user-wide in an isolated venv; the project never learns it exists.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
Run poetry once without installing it in a fresh project -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
```bash
uvx poetry
```

`uvx` is `uv tool run` — it resolves `poetry` on the fly, runs it, and discards the environment afterwards. Nothing is added to `pyproject.toml`, nothing lands on your PATH.

Use `uv add --dev poetry` instead when the whole team needs it pinned, and `uv tool install poetry` when you want it permanently on your own PATH.

### Question:
How do I add hypothesis and mypy as dev dependencies where the previous setup used Black and Flake8?

### Answer:
```bash
uv add --dev hypothesis mypy
```

`--dev` puts them in the `dev` dependency group in `pyproject.toml`, so `uv sync` installs them for contributors and `uv sync --no-dev` leaves them out of the production image.

Not `uv tool install` — that is user-wide and would not be pinned in `uv.lock` for anyone else.

### Question:
How do I run the linter over packages in a monorepo?

### Answer:
```bash
ruff check packages
```

To apply the fixes it can make automatically:

```bash
ruff check --fix packages
```

There is no `uv ruff` — `uv` manages environments and dependencies, `ruff` does the linting. Use `uv run ruff check packages` if you want it to run inside the project environment rather than off your PATH.

### Question:
Can you format packages and fix what can be fixed automatically in a fresh project?

### Answer:
```bash
ruff format packages
ruff check --fix packages
```

`ruff format` rewrites layout — spacing, quote style and where lines break. `ruff check --fix` is the linter, and it repairs a different class of problem: unused names, import ordering and deprecated idioms.

Run `format` first; a reformatted file can change which lines the linter flags.

### Question:
Set up ruff in pyproject.toml with a 88-character line limit targeting Python 3.12 that a contractor will hand back to us?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
```

`select` here turns on everything, then narrow with `ignore`. `target-version` tells the pyupgrade rules which syntax they are allowed to modernise to.

### Question:
Need to keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight tests/** where the previous setup used Black and Flake8. Show me.

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "DOC",    # docstring content rules, too noisy for now
    "E501",   # line length, the formatter already owns this
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S101", "ANN201"   # asserts and untyped test helpers are fine]
```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

### Question:
Need to make ruff treat `core` as first-party when sorting imports on a team of six. Show me.

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff]
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["I"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["core"]
combine-as-imports = true
```

Without `src`, a `src/` layout makes Ruff read `core` as third-party and sort it into the wrong block.

### Question:
What should I do to split our dev tooling into separate groups so CI installs only what it needs for a package with a src/ layout?

### Answer:
```toml
[dependency-groups]
dev = ["hypothesis", "mypy"]
test = ["pytest", "pytest-cov"]
docs = ["mkdocs", "mkdocs-material"]
```

```bash
uv sync --group test          # CI test job
uv sync --no-dev                # production image
```

`[dependency-groups]` is the PEP 735 standard table, so it is not uv-specific — other tools read it too.

### Question:
What should I do to make everyone on the team build against Python 3.12 and the same uv for an internal CLI tool?

### Answer:
```bash
uv python pin 3.12
```

```toml
[project]
requires-python = ">=3.12"

[tool.uv]
required-version = ">=0.5.0"
```

`uv python pin` writes `.python-version`, which `uv run` and `uv sync` both honour. `requires-python` is the constraint the resolver uses; `required-version` fails fast when someone's uv is too old to read the lockfile format.

### Question:
Point `pricing-engine` at our internal git repo without breaking the lockfile where the previous setup used Black and Flake8?

### Answer:
```toml
[project]
dependencies = ["pricing-engine"]

[tool.uv.sources]
pricing-engine = { git = "https://git.corp.example/pricing-engine", tag = "v0.14.2" }
```

`[tool.uv.sources]` is a TABLE keyed by package name, not a list. `pricing-engine` still appears in `[project.dependencies]` — the source table only overrides WHERE it is fetched from, so the metadata stays standard for anything that is not uv.

### Question:
Turn on type checking without failing the build on the legacy package for a package with a src/ layout. Config please.

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ty.src]
include = ["src"]

[tool.ty.rules]
possibly-unbound-attribute = "warn"

[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["src/compat/**"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"
```

```bash
uv run ty check
```

`[[tool.ty.overrides]]` is what keeps the strict setting on new code while the legacy tree stays quiet — better than lowering the global rule.

### Question:
Decide between `uv add --dev yt-dlp` and `uv tool install yt-dlp`. Config please.

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev yt-dlp

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install yt-dlp
```

`uv add --dev` makes `yt-dlp` part of what `uv sync` reconstructs for every contributor. `uv tool install` puts it on your PATH in its own environment and touches neither file — nothing is pinned for anyone else.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
Decide between `uv add --dev yt-dlp` and `uv tool install yt-dlp` for a library we publish to PyPI. Config please.

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev yt-dlp

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install yt-dlp
```

`uv add --dev` writes `yt-dlp` into `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, so a colleague who runs `uv sync` gets the identical version. `uv tool install` installs it user-wide in an isolated venv; the project never learns it exists.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

How do I decide between `uv add --dev black` and `uv tool install black` for a service that ships in a slim Docker image?

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
```

Split our dev tooling into separate groups so CI installs only what it needs for a library we publish to PyPI -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
```toml
[dependency-groups]
dev = ["mypy", "hypothesis"]
test = ["pytest", "pytest-cov"]
docs = ["mkdocs", "mkdocs-material"]
```

```bash
uv sync --group test          # CI test job
uv sync --no-dev                # production image
```

`[dependency-groups]` is the PEP 735 standard table, so it is not uv-specific — other tools read it too.

### Question:
What should I do to point `pricing-engine` at our internal git repo without breaking the lockfile where the previous setup used Black and Flake8?

### Answer:
```toml
[project]
dependencies = ["pricing-engine"]

[tool.uv.sources]
pricing-engine = { git = "https://github.com/acme/pricing-engine", tag = "v3.0.0-rc2" }
```

`[tool.uv.sources]` is a TABLE keyed by package name, not a list. `pricing-engine` still appears in `[project.dependencies]` — the source table only overrides WHERE it is fetched from, so the metadata stays standard for anything that is not uv.

### Question:
Replace black, isort and flake8 with ruff in one pass where the previous setup used Black and Flake8 -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
```bash
uv remove --dev black isort flake8
uv add --dev ruff
ruff check --fix .
ruff format .
```

```toml
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100          # what the old setup used

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B"]
```

Ruff's formatter is Black-compatible by design, so keeping `line-length` where Black had it makes the first reformat a near no-op instead of a diff across every file.

### Question:
Decide between `uv add --dev poetry` and `uv tool install poetry` that a contractor will hand back to us?

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev poetry

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install poetry
```

`uv add --dev` writes `poetry` into `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, so a colleague who runs `uv sync` gets the identical version. `uv tool install` gives you a personal copy on PATH that no lockfile describes.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

Run poetry once without installing it where the previous setup used Black and Flake8 -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
```bash
uvx poetry
```

`uvx` is `uv tool run` — it fetches `poetry` into a throwaway environment and runs it. Nothing is added to `pyproject.toml`, nothing lands on your PATH.

Use `uv add --dev poetry` instead when the whole team needs it pinned, and `uv tool install poetry` when you want it permanently on your own PATH.

```bash
uv add --dev pre-commit mypy
```

Not `uv tool install` — that is user-wide and would not be pinned in `uv.lock` for anyone else.

### Question:
Can you keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight tests/** on a team of six?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "ANN",    # annotations -- rolling out gradually
    "ISC001", # implicit string concat, conflicts with the formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["PLR2004", "SLF001"  # magic numbers and private access in tests]
```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

### Question:
Turn on type checking without failing the build on the compat package in a monorepo?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ty.src]
include = ["lib"]

[tool.ty.rules]
possibly-unbound-attribute = "warn"

[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["src/compat/**"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"
```

```bash
uv run ty check
```

`[[tool.ty.overrides]]` is what keeps the strict setting on new code while the legacy tree stays quiet — better than lowering the global rule.

### Question:
Can you format packages and fix what can be fixed automatically for a service that ships in a slim Docker image?

### Answer:
```bash
ruff format packages
ruff check --fix packages
```

`ruff format` rewrites layout — quotes, line breaks, trailing commas. `ruff check --fix` is the linter, and it repairs a different class of problem: dead imports, import order and legacy syntax.

Run `format` first; a reformatted file can change which lines the linter flags.

### Question:
Can you decide between `uv add --dev ruff` and `uv tool install ruff` for a library we publish to PyPI?

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev ruff

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install ruff
```

`uv add --dev` writes `ruff` into `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, so a colleague who runs `uv sync` gets the identical version. `uv tool install` installs it user-wide in an isolated venv; the project never learns it exists.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

Can you keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight tests/**/*.py in CI?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "D",      # docstring rules -- not enforcing these yet

]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004"  # assert and magic numbers are fine in tests]
```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

### Question:

### Question:
How do I keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight tests/** in CI?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "ANN",    # annotations -- rolling out gradually
    "ISC001", # implicit string concat, conflicts with the formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S101", "ANN201"   # asserts and untyped test helpers are fine]
```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

### Answer:
```bash
ruff format .
```

`ruff format` rewrites layout — spacing, quote style and where lines break. `ruff check --fix` is the linter, and it repairs a different class of problem: dead imports, import order and legacy syntax.

Run `format` first; a reformatted file can change which lines the linter flags.

### Question:

### Answer:
```bash
uvx ruff
```

`uvx` is `uv tool run` — it resolves `ruff` on the fly, runs it, and discards the environment afterwards. Nothing is added to `pyproject.toml`, nothing lands on your PATH.

Use `uv add --dev ruff` instead when the whole team needs it pinned, and `uv tool install ruff` when you want it permanently on your own PATH.

### Question:
How do I keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight test/** for a service that ships in a slim Docker image?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "ANN",    # annotations -- rolling out gradually
    "ISC001", # implicit string concat, conflicts with the formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"test/**" = ["S101", "PLR2004"  # assert and magic numbers are fine in tests]
```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

Format src and fix what can be fixed automatically in CI. Config please.

### Answer:
```bash
ruff format src
ruff check --fix src
```

`ruff format` rewrites layout — indentation, string quoting and line wrapping. `ruff check --fix` is the linter, and it repairs a different class of problem: unused names, import ordering and deprecated idioms.

Run `format` first; a reformatted file can change which lines the linter flags.

### Question:
Decide between `uv add --dev cookiecutter` and `uv tool install cookiecutter` for a service that ships in a slim Docker image -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev cookiecutter

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install cookiecutter
```

`uv add --dev` records `cookiecutter` as a project dependency, so the lockfile pins it and CI resolves the same build every time. `uv tool install` puts it on your PATH in its own environment and touches neither file — nothing is pinned for anyone else.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
Need to decide between `uv add --dev yt-dlp` and `uv tool install yt-dlp` in a monorepo. Show me.

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev yt-dlp

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install yt-dlp
```

`uv add --dev` writes `yt-dlp` into `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, so a colleague who runs `uv sync` gets the identical version. `uv tool install` puts it on your PATH in its own environment and touches neither file — nothing is pinned for anyone else.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
Need to decide between `uv add --dev poetry` and `uv tool install poetry`. Show me.

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev poetry

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install poetry
```

`uv add --dev` records `poetry` as a project dependency, so the lockfile pins it and CI resolves the same build every time. `uv tool install` puts it on your PATH in its own environment and touches neither file — nothing is pinned for anyone else.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
How do I keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight tests/**/*.py on a team of six?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "ANN",    # annotations -- rolling out gradually
    "ISC001", # implicit string concat, conflicts with the formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["S101", "PLR2004"  # assert and magic numbers are fine in tests]
```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

`ruff format` rewrites layout — indentation, string quoting and line wrapping. `ruff check --fix` is the linter, and it repairs a different class of problem: unused imports, unsorted imports, outdated syntax.

Run `format` first; a reformatted file can change which lines the linter flags.

How do I split our dev tooling into separate groups so CI installs only what it needs for a service that ships in a slim Docker image?

### Answer:
```toml
[dependency-groups]
dev = ["hypothesis", "ruff"]
test = ["pytest", "pytest-cov"]
docs = ["mkdocs", "mkdocs-material"]
```

```bash
uv sync --group test          # CI test job
uv sync --no-dev                # production image
```

`[dependency-groups]` is the PEP 735 standard table, so it is not uv-specific — other tools read it too.

### Question:
Point `auth-lib` at our internal git repo without breaking the lockfile. Config please.

### Answer:
```toml
[project]
dependencies = ["auth-lib"]

[tool.uv.sources]
auth-lib = { git = "https://github.com/acme/auth-lib", tag = "v3.0.0-rc2" }
```

`[tool.uv.sources]` is a TABLE keyed by package name, not a list. `auth-lib` still appears in `[project.dependencies]` — the source table only overrides WHERE it is fetched from, so the metadata stays standard for anything that is not uv.

### Question:
Replace black, isort, flake8 and bandit with ruff in one pass in CI. Config please.

### Answer:
```bash
uv remove --dev black isort flake8 bandit
uv add --dev ruff
ruff check --fix packages
ruff format .
```

```toml
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120          # what the old setup used

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B"]
```

because the formatter matches Black's output, holding `line-length` steady keeps the migration commit reviewable instead of touching every file.

```bash
ruff check worker/
```

### Question:
How do I format lib and fix what can be fixed automatically for a library we publish to PyPI?

### Answer:
```bash
ruff format lib
ruff check --fix lib
```

`ruff format` rewrites layout — quotes, line breaks, trailing commas. `ruff check --fix` is the linter, and it repairs a different class of problem: unused imports, unsorted imports, outdated syntax.

Run `format` first; a reformatted file can change which lines the linter flags.

### Question:
Decide between `uv add --dev yt-dlp` and `uv tool install yt-dlp` that a contractor will hand back to us. Config please.

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev yt-dlp

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install yt-dlp
```

`uv add --dev` makes `yt-dlp` part of what `uv sync` reconstructs for every contributor. `uv tool install` gives you a personal copy on PATH that no lockfile describes.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
Keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight tests/** for a library we publish to PyPI -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "D",      # docstring rules -- not enforcing these yet
    "COM812", # trailing-comma, conflicts with the formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["PLR2004", "SLF001"  # magic numbers and private access in tests]
```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

What should I do to make ruff treat `worker` as first-party when sorting imports for a library we publish to PyPI?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff]
src = ["lib", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["I"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["worker"]
combine-as-imports = true
```

Without `src`, a `lib/` layout makes Ruff read `worker` as third-party and sort it into the wrong block.

### Question:
Turn on type checking without failing the build on the compat package in a repo that still has a requirements.txt -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ty.src]
include = ["packages"]

[tool.ty.rules]
possibly-unbound-attribute = "warn"

[[tool.ty.overrides]]
include = ["src/thirdparty/**"]

[tool.ty.overrides.rules]
unresolved-attribute = "ignore"
```

```bash
uv run ty check
```

`[[tool.ty.overrides]]` is what keeps the strict setting on new code while the legacy tree stays quiet — better than lowering the global rule.

### Question:

### Question:
How do I decide between `uv add --dev ruff` and `uv tool install ruff` for a package with a src/ layout?

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev ruff

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install ruff
```

`uv add --dev` makes `ruff` part of what `uv sync` reconstructs for every contributor. `uv tool install` gives you a personal copy on PATH that no lockfile describes.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
Decide between `uv add --dev pgcli` and `uv tool install pgcli` in a repo that still has a requirements.txt -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev pgcli

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install pgcli
```

`uv add --dev` records `pgcli` as a project dependency, so the lockfile pins it and CI resolves the same build every time. `uv tool install` installs it user-wide in an isolated venv; the project never learns it exists.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
How do I keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight test/**?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "D",      # docstring rules -- not enforcing these yet
    "COM812", # trailing-comma, conflicts with the formatter
]

```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

### Question:
Can you format lib and fix what can be fixed automatically in a monorepo?

### Answer:
```bash
ruff format lib
ruff check --fix lib
```

`ruff format` rewrites layout — indentation, string quoting and line wrapping. `ruff check --fix` is the linter, and it repairs a different class of problem: unused names, import ordering and deprecated idioms.

Run `format` first; a reformatted file can change which lines the linter flags.

### Question:
How do I keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight tests/**/*.py in a fresh project?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "DOC",    # docstring content rules, too noisy for now
    "E501",   # line length, the formatter already owns this
]

```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

### Question:
Keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight tests/**/*.py for a library we publish to PyPI -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "D",      # docstring rules -- not enforcing these yet
    "COM812", # trailing-comma, conflicts with the formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["PLR2004", "SLF001"  # magic numbers and private access in tests]
```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
```

### Question:
Decide between `uv add --dev httpie` and `uv tool install httpie` for a library we publish to PyPI -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev httpie

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install httpie
```

`uv add --dev` writes `httpie` into `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, so a colleague who runs `uv sync` gets the identical version. `uv tool install` installs it user-wide in an isolated venv; the project never learns it exists.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
Keep ruff's broad rule set but silence the rules that fight test/** for a library we publish to PyPI. Config please.

### Answer:
```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "ANN",    # annotations -- rolling out gradually
    "ISC001", # implicit string concat, conflicts with the formatter
]

```

`per-file-ignores` is the part worth reaching for — it keeps the strict set everywhere else instead of globally disabling a rule because one directory trips it.

### Question:
Decide between `uv add --dev ruff` and `uv tool install ruff` in a repo that still has a requirements.txt. Config please.

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev ruff

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install ruff
```

`uv add --dev` makes `ruff` part of what `uv sync` reconstructs for every contributor. `uv tool install` puts it on your PATH in its own environment and touches neither file — nothing is pinned for anyone else.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.

### Question:
How do I split our dev tooling into separate groups so CI installs only what it needs in a fresh project?

### Answer:
```toml
[dependency-groups]
```
```toml
dev = ["ty", "mypy"]
test = ["pytest", "pytest-cov"]

```

```bash
uv sync --group test          # CI test job
```

`[dependency-groups]` is the PEP 735 standard table, so it is not uv-specific — other tools read it too.

### Question:
Decide between `uv add --dev ruff` and `uv tool install ruff` in CI -- what's the right way?

### Answer:
They do different jobs, so pick by who needs it:

```bash
# a tool THIS project's contributors run -> project dev group
uv add --dev ruff

# a tool YOU run anywhere, isolated from any project -> user-wide
uv tool install ruff
```

`uv add --dev` makes `ruff` part of what `uv sync` reconstructs for every contributor. `uv tool install` installs it user-wide in an isolated venv; the project never learns it exists.

There is no `--dev` flag on `uv tool`, and no `install` subcommand on `uv add`. If you want it reproducible for the team, it is `uv add --dev`.
